---
title: "The relation-looking attribute that must stay silent"
---

`linked-to` below looks relation-like, but it is **not** a catalog relation and
is deliberately outside the conservative one-edit radius used by `QND005`.
Unknown `.need` keys remain an open namespace for project metadata, so the
engine must not turn every relation-looking custom attribute into a warning.

There is therefore no `QND005`, no graph edge, and no automatic guess. The
value survives exactly as authored as the ordinary `linked-to` attribute.
This fixture is the negative boundary for the neighboring
`probable-relation-typo/` fixture, where `verifed-by` is only one edit away
from the real `verified-by` relation and does receive an advisory.

::: {.need #REQ-A type="functional-requirement" status="draft" linked-to="REQ-B"}
## Signed payloads

The service shall sign every payload it emits.

### Rationale

`linked-to` is intentional project metadata in this fixture. It must not be
reinterpreted as a relation merely because its name looks relation-like.
:::

::: {.need #REQ-B type="functional-requirement" status="draft"}
## Payload signing keys

A second object makes it obvious that the custom attribute does not create an
edge between the two requirements.
:::
